statement: For D_omega on l^2(Z^3) defined by D_omega delta_x=U_x delta_x, with iid U_x uniform[-1,1], every local spectral measure is atomic and D_omega has pure point spectral type. Yet for u_eta(E)=pi^(-1)Im<(delta_0),(D_omega-E-i eta)^(-1)delta_0>, sup_{eta>0,E in R} E u_eta(E)<=1/2, the averaged local measure has density (1/2)1_{[-1,1]}, and Ward's identity holds. For every realization, integral_R u_eta(E)^2 dE=1/(2 pi eta).
proof_or_counterexample: Each delta_x is an eigenvector; u_eta is the Poisson kernel centered at U_0. Integrating in U_0 bounds its mean by 1/2. Integrating its square over energy gives 1/(2 pi eta). Full derivation saved before paired proof.
remaining_gap: This refutes an inference from annealed first moments, not the actual Anderson conjecture with unit hopping. Independent mathematical review and served-model evidence remain pending.

statement: Let mu_omega be a measurable random probability measure, I a bounded open interval, 1<p<infinity and eta_n decrease to zero. If sup_n E integral_I (P_eta_n*mu_omega)^p dE<infinity, then mu_omega restricted to I has an Lp(I) density almost surely. For stationary countable-site self-adjoint operators, the bound at one site implies pure absolute continuity on I, by transferring the law to all basis spectral measures and intersecting countably many full-probability events.
assumptions: mu_omega is a positive probability measure
I is fixed and bounded open
bound uniform in n at fixed positive disorder when applied to Anderson
proof_or_counterexample: Fatou makes the pathwise liminf of Lp norms finite. Extract a bounded subsequence, use reflexivity, and identify its weak limit using Poisson approximate-identity convergence against C_c(I). Basis spectral projections eliminate singular spectrum. The p=1 variant is refuted by L01.
remaining_gap: The premise is unproved for the target; nonzero spectral mass in I must be proved separately. No GOE consequence. Sufficient condition, not a necessary characterization of all AC measures. Independent review pending.

statement: For H=A+lambda V on l^2(Z^3), unit adjacency A, lambda>0 and iid bounded real potentials with density rho and ||rho||infinity=M, let Sigma(z)=<h,(H^(0)-z)^(-1)h>, a=E+Re Sigma and b=eta+Im Sigma>0. Conditional on all sites other than 0, E[(pi^(-1)Im G_00)^2|cavity]<=M/(2 pi lambda b). Thus a uniform expected integral of b^(-1) on a fixed interval along eta_n->0 suffices for L02 with p=2. If V_0 is uniform[-1,1], the same conditional second moment is at least 1/(4 lambda pi^2 b) on {|a|+b<=lambda}.
assumptions: iid sites; only V_0 is independent of the cavity sigma-field
uniform[-1,1] law only for the lower bound
variance-one uniform slice obtained by replacing lambda with sqrt(3) times the primary-source coupling
proof_or_counterexample: Exact Schur complement G_00=(lambda V_0-a-i b)^(-1). Single-site integration uses integral_R b^2/(t^2+b^2)^2 dt=pi/(2b). Restrict integration to [a-b,a+b] for the uniform-law lower bound. No product of cavity-neighbor probabilities is used.
remaining_gap: Control of inverse cavity imaginary parts on resonant environments uniformly as eta->0 is unproved. b>=eta only gives the divergent bound O(eta^-1). No parent theorem or GOE proof.
